Flooding is possible from 07:15 pm to 11:15 pm on Saturday 24th October 26. 
Flooding for Christchurch Harbour and the tidal stretches of the Lower Stour and Avon is possible for the evening tide at 9.15pm on Saturday 24/10/26.  Stormy weather systems will cause sea levels to be higher than forecasted in the tide tables.  Sea spray overtopping is possible and high-water levels in the harbour are forecast.  A level of 1.29 mAOD is expected with Force 8 South Westerly wind.  Flooding to roads and low-lying land is possible and conditions can apply two hours either side of high tide. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   
This message will be updated by 2:30PM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.

A small amount of water may then flow or be directed westwards along Mill Lane towards residential property in Climping Street. This event will increase tide table values by 0.26 m. High tides today may lead to flooding. 
 
Flooding is possible from 4.15 pm to 11.15 pm on Saturday 24th October 26. . 
 
Spring tides will affect the whole of the East Coast of Dorset and particularly at Portland Harbour and Preston Beach at Weymouth. Other areas at risk include Swanage, Poole Harbour and at Christchurch Harbour. The forecast is for stormy weather over the weekend and into next week. Please consider activating any flood protection measures you may have and be careful along beaches, promenades, coastal footpaths and roads. 
 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.

We are closing flood gates at Maryport and Flimby. 
Avoid seafronts and harbours due to wave overtopping and spray containing debris.  
This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.
